title: SAE Feature Co-Activation Graphs: Are Harmful Features Clustered?

original_idea.body:
# SAE Feature Co-Activation Graphs: Are Harmful Features Clustered?

**Problem:** Whether safety-relevant features form a tight cluster vs being diffuse changes how a monitor should aggregate them.

**Direction:** Run a pretrained GPT-2-small SAE over a labeled benign/harmful corpus. Build a feature co-activation graph and measure whether safety-relevant features are more densely interconnected than random sets.

**Why it matters:** If harmful concepts co-activate tightly, a monitor can watch a compact cluster; if diffuse, single-feature monitors miss harm.

**Relevant context:** Feature Hedging (2025); Neuronpedia GPT-2 SAE features.
